SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 5 : Formula One's governing body has promised a full investigation into a software bug that caused chaos and forced the start of Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to be aborted with drivers feeling like they were in battery-powered cars made of Lego. Ferrari's seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's four-time champion and eventual race winner Max Verstappen were among several affected by the glitch on a formation lap after torrential rain and a long delay at Malaysia's steamy Sepang circuit.   Verstappen compared the experience to a 'Lego race' held at Silverstone before the British Grand Prix while Hamilton, the sport's most successful driver of all time, had to stop his car on track and re-start it in what he said was a career first. The episode was the latest in a difficult first season for the new era of cars and engines, with drivers at the pinnacle of motorsport unhappy since the opening race with the power units' increased electrical component and the need for energy management.

The governing FIA said afterwards that "an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars."  "As a result, the FIA technical department removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release distributed to all competitors during the race delay caused by heavy rain, enabling teams to make the necessary changes to the power unit before the start of the race. “This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or during the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue." The FIA's single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis told reporters the lack of pre-season testing in wet conditions had played a part in the chaos. "Some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely," he said. “That bug prevented the power from being redeployed, and for the cars to start again. "I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time, and not have such a situation." Sepang was the first race weekend of the season with wet conditions, although the track dried during the race. "Sometimes things fall through the net and people learn, and you do a better job next time,” said Tombazis.

(Writing by Alan Baldwin in London, editing by Pritha Sarkar)

Source: Reuters

Oct 4 : Title holders Portugal maintained their 100 per cent record in the Nations League with a 2-1 home win over Norway on Sunday to seal a place in the March quarter-finals and shift the focus further away from Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt exit from the squad last week. Goncalo Ramos netted 11 minutes from time to ensure Portugal secured a top-two finish in Group A4 as they moved six points ahead of second-placed Denmark, who won 1-0 at Wales. The Netherlands took over at the top of Group A2, after beating Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven, but only on goal difference from Greece, who held on grimly for a goalless draw at home to Germany in Thessaloniki. Portugal were still under a cloud from Ronaldo’s dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, although they were triumphant without him in Denmark last Thursday after he walked out on the squad, and continued their winning ways in Porto on Sunday.

Norway took the lead in the 36th minute from centre-back Kristoffer Ajer, who hit a dipping half-volley from the edge of the box. But if that effort was sumptuous, Joao Cancelo’s thrashing effort to equalise two minutes later was even more awe-inspiring. Ramos’ winner came off his calf after Joao Felix had headed across goal for him to score. “You need a lot of technical quality to beat Norway," said the Portugal coach. "We won without putting in a performance like the one against Denmark, but the important thing was the victory and qualification. I had a lot of belief in this team, but perhaps I didn’t expect us to have four wins from our first four games,” Jorge Jesus added. RED CARD SOURS PORTUGAL'S WIN Portugal’s win was soured by a red card for Francisco Conceicao four minutes from time. He gave the referee a cynical thumbs up after receiving a yellow card and was immediately handed his marching orders. Wales goalkeeper Danny Ward made several key saves to keep Denmark at bay in Cardiff, but then conceded a penalty with a foul on Gustav Isaksen, allowing Rasmus Hojlund to tuck away a 75th-minute penalty to win their tie.  The Netherlands, with captain Virgil van Dijk celebrating a 100th cap, went ahead against Serbia when Teun Koopmeiners’s 31st-minute freekick evaded all in the penalty area and crept into the corner. But the visitors were level within four minutes as Aleksa Terzic crossed for teenager Mihajlo Cvetkovic to rise over Koopmeiners and head in his first international goal. ZIRKZEE GRABS DUTCH WINNER It took until the 72nd minute to go back ahead when Denzel Dumfries’ low cross was turned back across the goal by Tijjani Reijnders, sliding in at the far post, and tapped in by Joshua Zirkzee, who received a late call-up to the Dutch squad last week.  Germany dominated away against Greece, but Jurgen Klopp’s inexperienced side could not find the net, and they have won only one of their first four games under the new coach. Austria needed a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Kosovo but still have a three-point lead at the top of Group B3 after the Republic of Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 behind closed doors in the Serbian town of Backa Topola. In Group D2, Abdulakh Khaybulayev’s first-half goal was enough to send Azerbaijan top of the standings with a 1-0 win over previously unbeaten Lithuania, while veteran Teddy Teuma came on as a second-half substitute to hand Malta a 1-0 home win over Andorra in Group D1.  (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; editing by Pritha Sarkar)

Source: Reuters

Oct 4 : Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon will testify at a New York City hearing on artificial intelligence, Bloomberg News reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Coxon will appear at the request of New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around the technology, the report said. Coxon quit Anthropic last month, issuing warnings that the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade" and accusing his former employer and OpenAI of "gambling with our lives." Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

Source: Reuters

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 4 : Lauren Hemp scored twice as Manchester City came from behind on two occasions to beat Arsenal 4-2 in the Women's Super League on Sunday, keeping the champions top of the table heading into the international break after a fifth straight win from their opening five matches. Arsenal went ahead through Lisa Baum in the 43rd minute, but City levelled when Hemp forced the ball home from a tight angle in first-half stoppage time. Alessia Russo put the Gunners back in front four minutes after the break but again City came back, Kerstin Casparij equalising in the 63rd minute before Hemp put them in front for the first time nine minutes later.  Striker Bunny Shaw sealed the three points in the 84th minute with her fifth goal of the season to condemn Arsenal, who are without a win since the opening day of the season, to their second straight defeat after losing 1-0 away to Chelsea last week.

The loss leaves Arsenal in 10th spot on five points from five games after a dismal start to the campaign.  Earlier in the afternoon, Sonia Bompastor's Chelsea thumped West Ham United 3-0 to put them into second place, two points behind City. They took the lead thanks to a Melvine Malard strike and added two late goals through Keira Walsh and Maika Hamano. London City Lionesses showed that they will be a force to be reckoned with in the title race, Alexia Putellas scoring twice in the first half of a 6-1 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur, who were left shell-shocked by the pressing of the visitors. Spurs had only conceded two goals in the first four outings, but they were hit for six as London City notched their third successive win in impressive fashion to move to third place on 12 points.  Charlton Athletic, who are still searching for their first point since being promoted, remain bottom of the 14-team table after a 5-1 hammering at the hands of Brighton & Hove Albion, with Kiko Seike scoring twice for the Seagulls.  Everton's strong start to the season continued with a 2-1 win over Birmingham City that lifts them to fifth spot in the table on nine points, two ahead of cross-town rivals Liverpool, who lost 1-0 to Manchester United on Saturday.

DURBAN, Oct 4 : South Africa fast bowler Anrich Nortje could make a remarkable return to first-class cricket after an absence of almost four years to help an injury-hampered South Africa attack in the first test against Australia, which starts in Durban on Friday. With fitness doubts over pace spearhead Kagiso Rabada and three other bowlers ruled out with hamstring injuries, Nortje is set to return to red-ball cricket for the first time since South Africa's test victory over West Indies in March 2023. That match, in which he took 5-36 in the first innings, was Nortje's last first-class appearance. A succession of injury setbacks, as he struggled with back and hip problems, subsequently led him to focus on the shorter formats, where bowling in brief spells has helped reduce the strain on his body.

The 32-year-old has evolved into a T20 specialist, but said on Sunday he had been working on his red-ball skills. "It's been quite a bit of a focus for me to try and execute skills with the red ball, to build loads gradually and in the right way try and get the overs up,” he told reporters on Sunday. “It's something that I've been doing for quite some time. There's been quite some effort put in to try and upskill again, and improve from where I left off.  "I'll be very excited if I can put my test cap on again. Growing up, it's the format you want to play. It's the motivation when you train," he added. Nortje has featured in 19 tests with a bowling average of 26.71 and regularly bowled at speeds in excess of 145kph – with his action taking a heavy toll on his body. TEST CRICKET BRINGS OUT EXTRA FIRE "You don't think of the tough times in T20 cricket. You just think about executing skills there, whereas in tests, you think about the tough times, the good times, the hard work and think that gets you through some sessions. "There's just that little bit of extra X-factor that comes out, or fire that comes out, and energy that comes out," Nortje added. "Guys want to do well, and everyone wants to perform. It is a big series." South Africa started an intra-squad match on Sunday and late Monday will cut their preliminary squad from 18 to 15, with Nortje expected to make the cut despite his lengthy absence. "The guys have grown quite a bit,” he said of the test side which has since gone on to win the World Test Championship, beating Australia in mid-2025. “They've played a lot and they've done really well. Hopefully, I can just add on to that. I'm very keen to get going and be on the park and try to do well for the country," Nortje added.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

Source: Reuters

Oct 4 : UAE supporters have provided an early taste of Gulf Cup final fever, snapping up seats on six charter flights to Jeddah in less than 10 minutes as excitement builds for Tuesday's title clash against Saudi Arabia. The rush began shortly after the UAE Football Association opened registration for fans wishing to travel to the Gulf Cup final, turning what was meant to be a routine booking process into a frantic race for seats. The association had arranged six aircraft to transport supporters to Saudi Arabia after the national team's qualification for the final, hoping to ensure a strong Emirati presence in the stands. Local media reported that all available seats were taken within minutes of registration opening at 1 p.m. UAE time. The surge in demand came a day after the UAE defeated Oman 1-0 in Jeddah to reach its first Gulf Cup final since 2018, reigniting hopes of ending a 13-year wait for regional glory.

With every seat claimed almost as soon as it became available, the rapid sellout offered an early indication of the atmosphere expected at King Abdullah Sports City on Tuesday, where a sizeable contingent of Emirati supporters is expected.

Oct 4 : When Lionel Messi makes his final appearance for Argentina on Tuesday, it will bring to an end a journey that began with the country's football authorities not even knowing his name and evolved into one of the most enduring relationships in sporting history. The farewell against Benin at Buenos Aires' Monumental stadium ends an international career spanning more than two decades, which began with Argentina scrambling to identify a teenage prodigy developing far from home. "He went through so many moments that they're really very different eras. At first he suffered enormously with the national team. He truly endured it," Argentine journalist and author Sergio Levinsky, who wrote "Messi and Everything Else", told Reuters. Messi moved to Barcelona as a teenager and, while Spain tried to persuade him to represent them, his own country barely knew he existed.

At the 2003 Under-17 World Cup in Finland, Spain beat Argentina 3-2 after extra time in the semi-finals. According to Levinsky, a young Cesc Fabregas, who scored twice and was Messi's teammate at Barcelona's La Masia academy, told Argentine delegates afterwards: "You lost to us because we've got your best player at Barcelona and he's a genius." Argentina youth coach Hugo Tocalli recalled a similar encounter. He said at the Ole Summit last month that Spain's head chef told him Argentina needed "a kid who plays in Barcelona" to win the tournament. Finding the boy from Rosario proved difficult. Argentine Football Association (AFA) employee Omar Souto tracked down the Messi family in Spain through a Rosario telephone directory, only to ask for "Leonardo". "His name isn't Leonardo, it's Lionel," Souto was told, according to the documentary "Messi: The Forgotten Tape". The confusion even extended to the paperwork. The AFA sent Barcelona a fax asking about a player called "Mecci," spelling the surname with a double "c" because officials believed he might be Italian, Levinsky said. A LOVE UNDER CONSTRUCTION After those complications, Messi played two under-20 friendlies for Argentina in 2004, his first appearances in the blue and white stripes. Yet scepticism lingered. At the 2005 Under-20 World Cup in the Netherlands, Messi began on the bench as Argentina lost their opening game. "There was strong resistance to calling up a kid who didn't play in the country," Levinsky said. "He had to fight against those early suspicions, against being considered a foreigner because he lived in Spain." He was later criticised for failing to reproduce his club form and labelled "pecho frio", lacking heart or fire, by some fans. A World Cup qualifier against Colombia in 2011 began to change that perception, as Messi helped Argentina rally from a goal down to win in difficult conditions. "He was exhausted, even vomiting, and he ended up winning," Levinsky said. "It was the first time fans saw him differently." The bond strengthened when Messi briefly retired after Argentina's penalty shootout defeat by Chile in the 2016 Copa America final. Rather than blame him, Argentines pleaded publicly for him to return. "People realised he was not responsible for the defeats. He was the one getting them to finals," Levinsky added. Under Lionel Scaloni, Messi became the undisputed leader of a new generation, guiding Argentina to two Copa America titles and the 2022 World Cup. His evolution into a more outspoken captain drew comparisons with Diego Maradona, but Levinsky said the usual debate between Argentina's two biggest icons missed the point. "It is Messi and Maradona," he added. "They were both geniuses in different eras." For Levinsky, Argentina's affection for Messi was not as immediate as it was for Maradona. It developed around a player whose upbringing and career unfolded largely abroad but who grew closer to supporters over time. "Messi was like suddenly finding out you have an 18-year-old son," Levinsky said. "You have to start loving him without having known he existed. It was a love under construction."

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Oct 4 : Daryz clinched a historic victory over Bay City Roller to win his second consecutive Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe at Longchamp on Sunday, the first colt to do so in nearly half a century.  Always prominent Bay City Roller defied his 28/1 odds to run a valiant race having hit the front two furlongs out under jockey Oisin Murphy, after running wide in the early stages. Still, Daryz proved to have too much class. Rounding the bend, last year's winner, who went off 7/4 favourite for trainer Francis-Henri Graffard, showed an incredible turn of foot and surged up the outside to pull clear of the pack and deny the battling Bay City Roller in the final stages of the race. Fancied three-year-old filly Diamond Necklace defied a wide draw to finish a credible third.  "What an amazing ride and what an amazing racehorse he is, he wears his heart on his sleeve and he has all the talent and all the ability to go with it," said Bay City Roller's trainer George Scott.

Europe's richest flat race the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe attracts the world's best middle-distance horses who compete for glory, and a share of the five-million-euro ($5.63 million) prize pot, at the storied Paris track. It is the pinnacle of many trainer's careers. Daryz's double is the first since the great mare Enable who won the race in 2017 and 2018 and stakes his claim as one of the world's greatest middle-distance racehorses. He is the first colt in 48 years to win back-to-back renewals of the race and his success cements the Aga Khan Studs as the Arc's most successful winning owners. Daryz is without a doubt a Longchamp specialist having won at the course three times already this year. The French superstar has amassed nearly three million pounds ($3.97 million) in prize money and his only subpar performance of the season came at Ascot when he was third to Ombudsman in the Group 1 Prince of Wales's Stakes.  The race rounds off a fantastic weekend for British trainer George Scott who scored a career best with a double on the first day of the meeting. Oct 4 : Elfyn Evans ended years of heartache, and a quarter-of-a-century wait for Britain, by finally winning the World Rally Championship (WRC) title with Toyota after a dramatic season finale in Sardinia on Sunday. The Welshman had been championship runner-up five times in the last six years but emerged triumphant after a  final Powerstage duel with teammate Oliver Solberg ended with the charging Swede crashing out two corners from the finish while on course to take the crown. Solberg, 25, ran wide and careered down a bank before getting the car back on the road. He still won the rally but lost the crucial bonus points on offer for the top five in the final stage. Evans, with co-driver Scott Martin at his side, became the first British world rally champion since Englishman Richard Burns in 2001 and only the third since Scottish driver Colin McRae became the nation's first in 1995.

END OF AN ERA FOR RALLYING  Sweden's Solberg, son of Norway's 2003 champion Petter, ended the season as runner-up. The final standings left Evans on 243 points, Solberg on 238 and Sami Pajari on 237 in what was also the end of an era for the sport with new regulations in force next year. "It hasn't sunk in. I was sure it was over. I didn't drive the best stage but threw everything at it but it wasn't clean. I feel for Oliver. He had an incredible weekend," said Evans, who completed his final run first and had to watch and wait to see whether he had done enough to take the title. "I don't really know what my reaction is, it's surreal with how it happened. It's a relief. It wouldn't be my proudest way of winning it, but it's job done," added the 37-year-old, who finished fifth in the gravel rally. Evans had started the rally - the final round after Saudi Arabia's finale was cancelled due to conflict in the region - 17 points clear of Finland's Pajari, also in a Toyota, and 21 clear of Solberg. The Swede took control of the rally on Saturday, knowing he had nothing to lose and all to gain, and started the final day 33.6 seconds clear of the field and the momentum swinging his way. That feeling was reinforced when Evans lost time changing a wheel on Sunday's penultimate stage, leaving the championship outcome hanging on the short final stage and the title going to which of the pair finished ahead of the other. Toyota had already won the manufacturers' championship.

Source: Reuters

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 4 : Lewis Hamilton said he had mixed emotions after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia where he started second on the grid but dropped to 18th when a tyre gamble went wrong before fighting to finish third in a chaotic, rain-hit race on Sunday. After rain delayed the start of the race by more than 90 minutes, Hamilton was one of the few drivers who switched from intermediate tyres to slicks on a track that was still drying. The Briton had a slow start and then found himself going backwards, falling as low as 18th, but he opted to stick with his strategy despite Ferrari calling him back into the pits for a tyre change. Hamilton then carved his way through the field as the track dried up while safety cars also came to his rescue, with the veteran eventually overtaking Red Bull's Isack Hadjar in the dying stages to secure a podium behind Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli.

"As a team, we ended up taking that soft (tyre) and at the end of the pit lane, these two (Verstappen and Antonelli) took off their (tyre) blankets and my heart just sank, because I knew straight away that we were in trouble," Hamilton told reporters. "As we pulled out, all the spray came out the back of Max's car and I was like, 'Okay, I'm done. My race is really in trouble'. "We made the decision to live with it. As everyone was overtaking me, they (Ferrari) said, 'Should we stop?' I said, 'No, we've already waited another 26 seconds. What's the difference'." But as the track dried and safety car deployments played into his hands, Hamilton began a remarkable recovery drive as he gave Hadjar chase for fourth place, before George Russell's retirement gave him a shot at a podium. "I just waited for the track to dry and once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great. Then after that, really good pit stops from my guys in the garage," Hamilton added. "And then a good strategy. So for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that's what was going to be the case. I'm really, really grateful." His teammate Charles Leclerc also salvaged fourth place for Ferrari and he conceded that was the best they could have achieved considering how much faster Red Bull and Mercedes were. "Honestly, the first part of the race, everything that could have gone wrong went wrong. And on the second part, everything that could have gone right went our way," Leclerc said. "So at the end of the day, I prefer it that way than the other way around. We were P4 today and I honestly think that with a normal race we would have finished P3 and P4. The two guys in front were just way too quick for us. "Lewis had quite a good pace. I struggled a lot with the car, which we're looking into. I had a good feeling on Friday, good feeling until Q2, and then Q3 I started to lose out. Today the race was very tricky."

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 4 : George Russell's Formula One title hopes took a crushing blow when his Mercedes ground to a halt with a power unit failure five laps from the finish, turning what looked like a certain podium into heartbreak at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday. The British driver was running in a strong position to claim valuable championship points when the second safety car emerged for Alex Albon's Williams, which was stuck in the gravel. But as the field prepared for a thrilling finale behind the safety car, Russell - who was third behind eventual race winner Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli - suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he climbed out. "You've almost got to laugh, it's beyond disappointment. It's just so many times this season it's happened. It's a real shame," Russell said.

"The podium looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race. But not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling." The retirement meant Russell's championship deficit grew from 66 points to 84 behind Antonelli. "I don't need to say I think it's (championship hopes) gone or whatever, but of course it's exceptionally unlikely and that's just the reality," Russell added. "I knew if I wanted to come back, I needed luck on my side... It's a real shame." Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirmed it was a power unit failure on Russell's car. "I'm so massively annoyed. I'm not in a happy place," Wolff said. "First of all we didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will." With the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc finishing third and fourth, Mercedes' lead in the constructors' standings is now 151 points. "We had such an advantage (with) two safety cars, you couldn't be more unlucky," Wolff added. "And to make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points. "So as much as I love to be here, when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences, to be honest."

SYDNEY, Oct 4 : Dual-code international winger Mark Nawaqanitawase scored two tries as the Sydney Roosters edged the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in the National Rugby League final on Sunday, securing the foundation club a 16th title. Nawaqanitawase, who could represent Australia at both the league and union World Cups over the next 12 months, crossed either side of halftime to help crush Newcastle hopes of a massive upset in front of a crowd of 80,814 at Stadium Australia. Newcastle were looking to take the title back to their industrial port city for the first time since 2001 and scored the first two tries of the contest through Francis Manuleleua and skipper Kalyn Ponga to take an early 12-0 lead. Nawaqanitawase, playing the final game of his two-year stint at the Roosters before his return to rugby union, cut the deficit from a clever kick and chase five minutes before the break, however.

Newcastle defended several sets on their own line at the start of the second half but Roosters centre Billy Smith forced his way over in the 47th minute for a converted try that locked up the scores at 12-12. Sam Walker put the Sydney side in front for the first time with a penalty seven minutes later, and Nawaqanitawase added his second try in the right corner before the hour mark to extend the lead to 18-12. Experienced five-eighth Daly Cherry-Evans, playing his last NRL game before his switch to England's Super League, slotted a field goal to extend the advantage to seven points but the Knights found a second wind in the remaining 11 minutes. Summoning the spirit of last week's sensational win over the Penrith Panthers with 12 men that got them to the final, they forced their way upfield and winger Greg Marzhew crossed for a converted try that made it a one-point game with four minutes on the clock. The Roosters, one of the two clubs remaining from the first season of what became the NRL in 1908, held on, however, to secure their first title since 2019 and fourth under long-term coach Trent Robinson. "Credit to the Knights, they fought for 80 minutes there," said Nawaqanitawase. "This is going to last me a lifetime, it's sad to go but I love everyone here, I love all the boys, and let's celebrate this win, far out."
